material_units.source_text:
Key equation — The exponential as a limit, and two inequalities
      
        $$e^{x}=\lim_{n\to\infty}\Big(1+\frac xn\Big)^{n},\qquad 1+x\le e^{x}\ \ (x\in\mathbb R),\qquad \ln x\le x-1\ \ (x\gt0).$$
        $(1+\frac1n)^n=2.5937,\ 2.7048,\ 2.7169$ for $n=10,100,1000$ ($e=2.71828$), and $(1-\frac1n)^n=0.3487,\ 0.3660,\ 0.3677$ ($1/e=0.3679$). Proof of the inequalities. $\phi(x)=e^x-1-x$ has $\phi'(x)=e^x-1$, negative for $x\lt0$ and positive for $x\gt0$, so $\phi\ge\phi(0)=0$. Replacing $x$ by $x-1$ gives $x\le e^{x-1}$; take logarithms. $\blacksquare$
